sourceOccurrences.label: Fractional coordinate weights and convolution identities
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Independent symmetric-difference Lp construction in place of the source's directional pointwise fractional-transform estimates
sourceOccurrences.note: The strict weight and power-counting conditions are explicit. Non-even input-moment endpoints and the sharper middle-diagram estimates are not identified with the source.

sourceOccurrences.label: Exact non-even input-moment endpoint
sourceOccurrences.relationship: The highest-derivative separation is retained; an integrated-difference Lp argument supplies the exact input-moment endpoint
sourceOccurrences.note: The endpoint uses only the stated real K-moment. Strict dimensional power counting is retained; no directional pointwise correspondence or numerical dimension claim.

sourceOccurrences.label: Weighted middle diagram from direct Lp estimates
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Independent Young and Holder estimate for the unweighted core, with heat regularization identifying the spatial sum
sourceOccurrences.note: For d>=7 and the stated real K-moment/gap hypotheses, the middle diagram is finite for 0<=beta<=K and beta<d-2. This is an additional estimate, not a source erratum or a directional pointwise correspondence.

sourceOccurrences.label: Directional fractional density estimate
sourceOccurrences.relationship: The symmetric-difference formula gives a pointwise majorant that implies the source directional bound under the explicit integer-input moment condition
sourceOccurrences.note: The weight s is positive and noninteger, ceil(s)<=K, and s+2<d. This pointwise assertion is distinct from the exact noninteger-moment Lp endpoint ENZ7.

proofUses.reason: Norm integrability of symmetric differences permits interchange with an inverse Fourier coefficient; scaling the cosine integral gives the absolute fractional multiplier.
Rescaled quotient regularity and a split around the shifted singularities give the translation gain needed by the fractional multiplier.
Holder makes the density product integrable; positive Fejer coefficients and monotone convergence identify the real-weighted spatial convolution.
Absolute convergence and Tonelli bound the integrated Fourier modulus by the exact weighted coefficient sum.
Isolate the highest derivatives, integrate their moduli using the exact moment, and apply the coefficient-interchange calculation under directly established norm integrability.
Young and Holder reduce the two-frequency core to a torus power convolution; dimension seven permits an arbitrarily small power loss.
The weighted density pairs with the middle core in dual Lp spaces; positive heat smoothing preserves the infrared majorant and identifies the full nonnegative spatial sum.

Split the symmetric-difference integral at the frequency distance; local derivatives control short shifts and a one-dimensional integral controls longer shifts. Fubini identifies the representative and the anisotropic majorant gives the Lp range.
